summary: A hand-built octagonal wooden tower of 1856 on Birch Point, moved inland in 1946 to escape erosion and still lit at the mouth of Chaleur Bay.

notes_for_editor: Keeper dates after 1877 come from Lighthouse Friends (secondary); only Rivers (1901 table) and Robichaud (1906 table) were confirmed in Marine Branch tables, matched by column position in OCR text. David Bell's date is unknown (placed at 1877 only as a floor). Characteristic: record says Oc W 5s, Wikipedia says Fl G 5s, CCG list text was garbled; not stated in story. Access season differs between Lighthouse Friends and Rowlett. A 1910 report lists payment for 'Services of R. Rivers, keeping light at Miscou, N.B., in 1899' which is unexplained and unused. The Marine Branch 1910-volume page 65 printed page number is unconfirmed, so cited by scan page. No wrecks tied to the station were found; Canadian newspapers not searched. Checker 2026-10-27: Rivers and Robichaud table rows confirmed on the page images (A.1902 printed p.148; A.1907 printed p.171). Lens alteration dated 1908 (FY to 31 Mar 1909 report; LF says 1908).
